The '''2013 season''' was the '''Portland Thorns{{'}}''' inaugural season in the newly created [[National Women's Soccer League]] (NWSL), the top division of women's [[United States soccer league system|professional soccer in the United States]]. The Thorns ended the 22-game regular season in third place with a 10-6-6 record, qualifying them for the NWSL playoffs. In their semi-final game the team beat [[FC Kansas City]] 3-2 in [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]], qualifying them to play [[Western New York Flash]] in the championship. The Thorns beat the Flash 2–0, making Portland Thorns FC the NWSL champion.

==Background==
[[File:Portland Thorns.JPG|thumb|in 2013]]
The league's founding was announced on November 21, 2012, with Portland as a host for one of eight teams.<ref name="soccer wire league">{{cite web|title=U.S. Soccer to announce new women’s professional league today|url=http://www.soccerwire.com/news/u-s-soccer-to-announce-new-womens-professional-league-today/|work=Leagues|publisher=Soccer Wire|access-date=14 December 2012|date=November 21, 2012|archive-date=28 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140428042951/http://www.soccerwire.com/news/u-s-soccer-to-announce-new-womens-professional-league-today/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="pbj league">{{cite news |last=Giegerich |first=Andy |title=Women's pro soccer coming to Portland |url= http://www.bizjournals.com/portland/news/2012/11/21/womens-pro-soccer-coming-to-portland.html |access-date=14 December 2012|newspaper=[[Portland Business Journal]]|date=November 21, 2012}}</ref> At that time it was announced by [[Portland Timbers]]' owner [[Merritt Paulson]] that the Timbers would own the team.<ref name="pbj league"/>

The chosen team, Portland Thorns FC, was announced on December 13, 2012, accompanied by the unveiling of its logo.<ref name="pbj name">{{cite news|last=Siemers|first=Erik|title=Timbers name new women's club Portland Thorns|url=http://www.bizjournals.com/portland/blog/2012/12/timbers-name-new-womens-club-portland.html|access-date=14 December 2012|newspaper=Portland Business Journal|date=December 13, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Manning|first=Rob|title=Women's Soccer Team To Be Named 'Portland Thorns'|url=http://www.opb.org/news/article/womens-soccer-team-to-be-named-portland-thorns/|access-date=14 December 2012|work=Oregon Public Broadcasting|date=December 13, 2012|archive-date=December 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208162725/http://www.opb.org/news/article/womens-soccer-team-to-be-named-portland-thorns/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Arnold|first=Geoffrey C.|title=Portland Thorns: Women's professional soccer team unveils name, logo|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/timbers/index.ssf/2012/12/portland_thorns_womens_profess.html|access-date=14 December 2012|newspaper=[[The Oregonian]] |date= December 13, 2012}}</ref> Both the name and logo were intended to invoke Portland's nickname of the [[Nicknames of Portland, Oregon#City of Roses|Rose City]].<ref name="pbj name"/><ref name="soccer wire name">{{cite web|title=Portland women’s pro team unveils "Thorns FC" as identity|url=http://www.soccerwire.com/news/12129/|work=Clubs|publisher=Soccer Wire|access-date=14 December 2012|date=December 13, 2012|archive-date=27 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140227114739/http://www.soccerwire.com/news/12129/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[Cindy Parlow|Cindy Parlow Cone]] was announced as the first head coach on December 19, 2012.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cindy Parlow Cone hired as Portland Thorns FC coach|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/timbers/index.ssf/2012/12/cindy_parlow_cone_hired_as_por_1.html|access-date=20 December 2012|newspaper=The Oregonian|date=December 19, 2012}}</ref>

== Roster ==
In the [[National Women's Soccer League]]'s (NWSL) inaugural season, the eight founding clubs filled out their rosters through numerous mechanisms. First, teams are allocated national team players from the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Next, teams go through the NWSL College Draft, a free agency period, the NWSL Supplemental Draft, and the signing of Discovery Players.<ref>{{cite web|title=Frequently Asked Questions: NWSL Roster Procedures|url=http://www.nwslsoccer.com/News/694142.html|publisher=NWSL|access-date=May 20, 2013|date=January 18, 2013}}</ref>

== Player Transactions ==
=== National Team Player Allocation ===
On January 11, 2013, the league held its player allocation for the national team players, with Portland receiving seven players: [[Rachel Buehler]], [[Tobin Heath]], [[Karina LeBlanc]], [[Alex Morgan]], [[Marlene Sandoval]], [[Luz Saucedo]], and [[Christine Sinclair]].<ref name="national team allocation"/> On January 23, 2013, Heath signed a six-month contract with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C. (Ladies)|Paris Saint-Germain]] and expected to join the Thorns FC once the French club's season is concluded.<ref name="HeathPSG"/> On March 21, 2013, Sandoval and Saucedo, the two allocated [[Mexico national football team|Mexico national team]] [[defender (association football)|defenders]], were removed from the team roster, due to an injury and decision by the [[Mexican Football Federation]], respectively.<ref>{{cite web|title=Portland Thorns FC: Mexican Players Luz Saucedo and Marlene Sandoval Removed from Roster|url=http://www.stumptownfooty.com/2013/3/21/4133576/portland-thorns-fc-mexican-players-removed-from-roster|publisher=stumptownfooty.com|access-date=March 21, 2013|date=March 21, 2013}}</ref>

=== National Women's Soccer League College Draft ===
Each team in the NWSL got to pick once per round, with the draft order based on how well each team did in allocation. The Thorns picked eighth (last) in each round.<ref name="Discovery" />

=== Supplemental Draft Picks ===
Any player that wasn’t selected in the NWSL College Draft, and was done with her college eligibility, was eligible for the NWSL Supplemental Draft. The draft lasted six rounds. Again, the Thorns selected eighth (last) in each round.<ref name="Discovery" />
